docs/limits/current-limitations.md:1:# Current limitations
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:2:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:3:These constraints describe the active unified discovery system.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:4:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:5:## Discovery quality remains corpus-bound
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:6:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:7:Current judged corpora cover only a fraction of possible languages, repository layouts, and development tasks. Passing Grimoire, Lexicon, Arcana, or agent-discovery cases does not establish equivalent recall elsewhere.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:8:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:9:Measured benefit is task-shaped. Broad architectural investigations can improve substantially, while exact lookups and short named call chains may remain faster with direct shell inspection. Grimoire is an optional discovery aid inside a normal repository workflow, not a requirement for every query.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:10:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:11:Exact source, BM25 source, document, symbol, and relationship lanes can fail independently. Evaluate them separately before attributing a missed investigation to the interface as a whole.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:12:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:13:## Independent lanes are not a global answer ranking
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:14:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:15:Grimoire deliberately does not merge heterogeneous evidence into one score. The consumer must decide whether implementation, documentation, symbols, or graph relationships are most useful for the current task.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:16:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:17:Per-lane rank is meaningful only inside that lane. Scores from different providers are not calibrated against one another.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:18:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:19:## Source excerpts are bounded
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:20:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:21:Search results include compact source excerpts to reduce unnecessary inspection calls. Excerpts are capped and may omit relevant surrounding context. Full evidence still requires `inspect` on the returned handle.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:22:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:23:## Documentation can be stale
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:24:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:25:Document results include freshness and provenance metadata where available, but relevance does not prove that a document still matches implementation. Current source remains the authority for executable behavior.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:26:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:27:## Relationship discovery is intentionally local
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:28:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:29:The search relationship lane returns bounded direct relationships around discovered symbols. It is not an exhaustive transitive graph query. Use `trace` for paths and `impact` for bounded dependents.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:30:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:31:When Arcana is unavailable, Lexicon relationship facts provide a narrower fallback. Unsupported or unresolved language constructs can still omit edges.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:32:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:33:## Structural components remain optional runtime dependencies
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:34:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:35:Lexicon and Arcana retain independent executables, state formats, and publication lifecycles. Missing, stale, timed-out, or incompatible structural state produces warnings while exact, source, and document discovery continue when possible.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:36:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:37:Grimoire prepares and aligns available state but does not supervise provider daemons.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:38:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:39:Arcana now accepts Lexicon's C-family macro-specific unresolved reasons and preserves unknown unresolved-reason labels. Unknown node kinds degrade to `symbol`, while records with unknown relation labels are skipped because Arcana cannot safely invent graph semantics. These degradations are loud and persistent, but the resulting graph can be incomplete until Arcana learns the new relation.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:40:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:41:## Semantic source boundaries depend on Lexicon coverage
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:42:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:43:Prepared source uses Lexicon declaration spans when current facts are available. Unsupported files, omitted constructs, stale state, ambiguous overlaps, and source outside declarations retain fallback line-window chunks.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:44:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:45:Nested declarations are reduced to non-overlapping leaf spans. Oversized semantic declarations are split at the hard token ceiling.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:46:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:47:## Prepared state is fully materialized
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:48:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:49:Prepared source snapshots and lexical postings are decoded into memory. There is no lazy shard reader or long-lived resident retrieval service for very large repositories.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:50:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:51:## File eligibility is fixed
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:52:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:53:Supported extensions and extensionless names are compiled into Grimoire. Repositories can add ignore rules and explicit exclusions but cannot currently register new file classes or generated-content classifiers.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:54:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:55:## Exact recovery has a scanning fallback
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:56:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:57:Identifier-aware postings localize most exact searches. Queries with no lexical token, such as punctuation-only literals, still fall back to scanning prepared chunks to preserve exact behavior.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:58:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:59:## Managed model setup is Windows x64 only
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:60:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:61:`grimoire model setup` installs pinned CPU, Vulkan, or CUDA `llama.cpp` artifacts only on Windows x64. Other platforms require a compatible runtime and local model configured externally.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:62:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:63:Backend detection cannot guarantee the fastest or most stable backend for every device and driver.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:64:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:65:## The embedding service is external process state
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:66:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:67:`grimoire model serve` is blocking. Grimoire does not supervise or restart it as a daemon. Exact, source, symbol, and deterministic graph discovery remain available without embeddings. Document vectors and optional semantic graph entry points require a compatible live endpoint.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:68:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:69:## The Go native vector loader is Windows-only
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:70:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:71:The Rust vector engine is portable, but the production Go dynamic-library loader currently targets a Windows DLL. On unsupported platforms the document lane remains BM25-only.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:72:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:73:## Document vector search is exact float32 scanning
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:74:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:75:The current snapshot stores aligned `float32` vectors and performs exact inner-product search. It does not use quantized or approximate-nearest-neighbour indexes. This is deterministic but may become material for very large document corpora.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:76:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:77:## Immutable vector objects are not garbage-collected
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:78:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:79:Replaced document sections disappear from current manifests and snapshots, but immutable vector objects remain available for reuse. There is no reachability-based cleanup across retained snapshots.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:80:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:81:## Object ingestion is serialized
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:82:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:83:Embedding requests may overlap, but native object ingestion is serialized. Increasing endpoint concurrency can increase CPU, GPU, and memory pressure without removing persistence cost.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:84:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:85:## State maintenance is request-driven
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:86:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:87:Grimoire does not continuously watch repositories. Discovery defaults to refresh-if-needed preparation. Documentation vectors remain explicit build artifacts, and freshness checks prevent silently using mismatched snapshots.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:88:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:89:Initial preparation can dominate a first query because source, Lexicon, Arcana, and documentation state may all need alignment. Repeated `force-refresh` requests can erase the efficiency benefit of progressive discovery.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:90:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:91:## Investigation sessions store evidence, not reasoning
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:92:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:93:Sessions deduplicate returned nodes, ranges, documents, relationships, and paths. They do not preserve an agent's private reasoning or guarantee that two semantically equivalent queries map to identical evidence handles.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:94:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:95:## Release workflow is deliberately conservative
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:96:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:97:The root test, build, and release workflow defaults to one worker across Go and Cargo to prevent uncontrolled CPU fan-out. `--jobs N` is an explicit operator choice and can still overload a machine when set too high.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:98:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:99:## Diagnostics and compatibility are pre-release
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:100:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:101:Human-readable errors, diagnostic codes, JSON error envelopes, exit-code classes, CLI spelling, and prepared/vector state migration policy are not yet stable release promises.
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:102:
docs/limits/current-limitations.md:103:The current public discovery schema is `grimoire.discovery.v1`. Consumers must reject unsupported schemas rather than infer compatibility from field presence.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:1:# Roadmap
docs/planning/roadmap.md:2:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:3:This page contains work that is not yet complete. Implemented behavior is documented elsewhere.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:4:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:5:## Completed foundation
docs/planning/roadmap.md:6:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:7:- Lexicon and Arcana consolidated into the Grimoire repository while retaining independent applications, state, protocols, and specialist commands.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:8:- Grimoire namespaced Lexicon and Arcana administrative commands.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:9:- Content-addressed prepared source state with deterministic exact and BM25 retrieval.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:10:- Separate documentation indexing with BM25 and optional vectors.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:11:- Lexicon-grounded symbols and Arcana-backed direct relationships, trace, paths, and impact.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:12:- Stable snapshot-qualified handles and exact follow-up inspection.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:13:- Independent exact, source, document, symbol, and relationship limits.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:14:- Automatic aligned preparation across Grimoire, Lexicon, Arcana, and documentation state.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:15:- Persistent investigation sessions with evidence deduplication.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:16:- Managed local embedding runtime commands and Lodestone-backed optional vector state.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:17:- Root build, test, subset installation, deterministic packaging, release checksums, and GitHub release workflow.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:18:- Combined release bundles containing provider binaries, runtime adapters, native library, and canonical Grimoire agent skill.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:19:- Repository-owned retrieval, graph, documentation, and end-to-end agent evaluation.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:20:- Retired context-package compiler, query-shape, assembly, curation, and package-fitting paths removed from the active CLI and MCP product.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:21:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:22:## Near-term priorities
docs/planning/roadmap.md:23:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:24:1. Run the remaining source-plus-rationale task in the hidden-rubric version 2 agent suite and consolidate the five-task conclusion.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:25:2. Add release-path contract fixtures that carry C-family macro reasons and deliberately unknown labels through Lexicon, Arcana, and Grimoire warning propagation.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:26:3. Use the provider and state-overhead timing buckets to target remaining first-use preparation cost without weakening alignment or determinism.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:27:4. Calibrate compact search defaults, excerpt caps, duplicate-payload references, and degraded-provider response bounds against end-to-end agent outcomes.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:28:5. Expand judged corpora across repositories, languages, sizes, and task categories.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:29:6. Add stable machine-readable diagnostic codes and documented exit classes.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:30:7. Improve installation verification and host-specific MCP setup guidance as supported hosts stabilize.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:31:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:32:## Agent discovery quality
docs/planning/roadmap.md:33:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:34:- Add benchmark repetitions and confidence intervals for task-shape comparisons.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:35:- Measure time to first required evidence separately from final completion.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:36:- Attribute model cost to Grimoire output, direct source reads, shell search, and repeated evidence.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:37:- Add judged cross-language and generated-contract tasks.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:38:- Add negative-claim cases that require warning, truncation, and provider-coverage handling.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:39:- Improve stopping guidance only when measured agent behavior shows unnecessary discovery calls.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:40:- Prevent source/lexical fallback from expanding unboundedly when Arcana is unavailable.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:41:- Improve canonical-handle transfer so final evidence ranges match inspected ranges exactly.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:42:- Preserve the rule that agents may stop using Grimoire when direct inspection becomes cheaper.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:43:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:44:## Prepared-state maintenance
docs/planning/roadmap.md:45:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:46:- Add optional repository watching or Warlock-fed change events without making one-shot commands depend on a daemon.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:47:- Add lazy or bounded prepared-state reads for very large repositories.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:48:- Make file eligibility and generated-content policy configurable without weakening permanent state exclusions.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:49:- Calibrate semantic declaration chunking against judged retrieval and downstream-agent token use.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:50:- Improve preparation diagnostics so source, Lexicon, Arcana, and documentation costs are separately visible.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:51:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:52:## Retrieval and evidence lanes
docs/planning/roadmap.md:53:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:54:- Calibrate document BM25/vector behavior on external rationale-discovery tasks.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:55:- Improve direct relationship seed matching through judged task-shaped cases.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:56:- Add conflict and provenance diagnostics across source, documentation, Lexicon, and Arcana evidence.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:57:- Add external evidence providers only behind concrete, independently testable interfaces.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:58:- Define a stable external provider contract after current integrations settle.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:59:- Keep heterogeneous lanes independently ranked unless judged failures demonstrate a need for another explicit contract.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:60:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:61:## Vector-engine work
docs/planning/roadmap.md:62:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:63:- Add safe reachability-based immutable-object cleanup.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:64:- Add non-Windows Go dynamic-library loaders and release packaging.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:65:- Benchmark float32 against float16 and int8 encodings.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:66:- Optimize exact-scan kernels only when measurements show material benefit.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:67:- Consider approximate indexing only when exact search is no longer acceptable and exact fallback remains available.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:68:- Evaluate a more efficient ingestion boundary after measuring serialized persistence cost.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:69:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:70:## Distribution and compatibility
docs/planning/roadmap.md:71:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:72:- Decide whether former Arcana and Lexicon repositories should become automated compatibility mirrors.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:73:- Define canonical module and package import paths before a stable release.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:74:- Add repository-wide contribution guidance.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:75:- Define prepared-index, documentation-vector, Arcana-vector, Lexicon, Arcana, and embedding-runtime migration policy.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:76:- Add managed embedding runtime artifacts for additional platforms.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:77:- Add Warlock lifecycle integration for component discovery and state maintenance while keeping components independently usable.
docs/planning/roadmap.md:78:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:79:## Release gates
docs/planning/roadmap.md:80:
docs/planning/roadmap.md:81:Establish measured release gates for:

arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:1:# Lexicon ingestion boundary
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:2:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:3:Arcana consumes Lexicon snapshot contract v1 and compacts its durable identities into a packed repository graph. Binary v1 fact objects are the normal snapshot transport: Arcana verifies their exact content hashes, decodes their node, edge, and unresolved sections into typed records, and does not reconstruct JSONL. Legacy canonical JSON fact objects and the complete JSONL importer remain available for migration and diagnostics.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:4:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:5:## Identity boundary
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:6:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:7:Lexicon owns cross-tool SHA-256 node identities. Arcana stores each full Lexicon identity in the catalogue, hashes it into an internal 64-bit `NodeKey`, checks for compaction collisions during import, and assigns dense packed `NodeId` values during compilation. Dense IDs are snapshot-local and must never escape as durable cross-tool identities. Lexicon file content IDs are compacted for Arcana's internal change detection.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:8:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:9:Arcana continues to read its legacy TSV facts during migration, but no language adapter is owned by this repository.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:10:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:11:## Preserved semantics
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:12:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:13:Arcana accepts the common Lexicon node and relation vocabulary, including:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:14:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:15:- interfaces, traits, constructors, and parameters;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:16:- definite `calls` and conservative `possible-calls` as separate relations;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:17:- conversions, implementations, inheritance, trait use, overrides, reads, writes, and annotations;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:18:- interstack `http-endpoint`, `message-channel`, and `config-key` nodes;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:19:- `calls-endpoint`, `handled-by`, `publishes`, `consumes`, and `reads-config` relationships;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:20:- unresolved references with source spans and candidate metadata.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:21:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:22:Source spans are preserved in the catalogue and unresolved-reference store. Explicit file ownership drives Arcana's file-scoped replacement model. Binary record attributes are length-prefixed, so Arcana can skip arbitrary Lexicon `attributes` without parsing or persisting them; adding a provenance sidecar later will not require changing graph identity.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:23:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:24:## Forward compatibility and warnings
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:25:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:26:Arcana does not reject an otherwise valid Lexicon snapshot solely because a newer adapter emits an unrecognized semantic label:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:27:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:28:- known unresolved-reason labels remain typed, including the C-family macro reasons `unsupported-macro-expansion`, `macro-argument-mismatch`, `macro-expansion-cycle`, and `macro-expansion-depth`;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:29:- unknown unresolved-reason labels are preserved verbatim and remain queryable and visible in statistics;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:30:- unknown node kinds are conservatively represented as `symbol` so their identities and recognized relationships remain available;
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:31:- edge and unresolved-reference records with unknown relation labels are skipped because Arcana cannot safely invent graph semantics for them.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:32:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:33:Every degradation is deduplicated and reported as an `arcana sync WARNING`. The warnings are also written to the immutable Arcana snapshot as `compatibility.warnings`, and Grimoire repository status promotes them into its top-level warnings. Empty or structurally malformed required fields remain hard errors.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:34:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:35:## Snapshot synchronization
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:36:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:37:`arcana sync` resolves Lexicon's atomic `CURRENT` pointer, verifies the content-addressed snapshot manifest and every referenced fact object, and compares file object identities with the Lexicon snapshot consumed by the previous Arcana state. Added, changed, and removed file-object paths become Arcana's file-scoped replacement set. Any language-level shared-object change conservatively forces a packed rebuild, including when file objects changed in the same snapshot.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:38:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:39:Arcana stores immutable graph states under `.arcana/snapshots/<lexicon-snapshot-digest>/`. All sync writers share `.arcana/LOCK`, and `.arcana/CURRENT` is replaced atomically only after the new state verifies. The repository manifest identifies Lexicon as the adapter and records the consumed Lexicon snapshot ID as its adapter version, while a `lexicon.snapshot` sidecar makes the relationship explicit.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:40:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:41:When node identities remain unchanged, Arcana emits one cumulative overlay against the packed base. Node additions or removals, unusable prior state, unsupported incremental ownership, or any incremental planning failure fall back to a complete packed rebuild. This choice is internal; callers invoke the same `sync` operation in every case.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:42:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:43:`arcana sync --register` writes a versioned command definition under `.lexicon/consumers/`. Lexicon invokes that one-shot command after every successful manual or daemon-triggered scan. The event only reduces latency: immutable snapshots remain the durable handoff, so Arcana can also catch up later through an explicit `arcana sync`.
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:44:
arcana/docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md:45:Scoped Lexicon `mode=incremental` JSONL streams remain invalid as complete import input. Arcana derives incremental scope from verified snapshot manifests rather than accepting a partial stream without its surrounding snapshot state.
arcana/README.md:1:# Arcana
arcana/README.md:2:
arcana/README.md:3:> **Canonical source:** Arcana now lives inside the [Grimoire repository](https://github.com/Lokee86/grimoire) under `arcana/`. It remains an independently buildable Rust application, CLI, protocol, and reusable graph engine.
arcana/README.md:4:
arcana/README.md:5:Arcana is the repository-graph component of Grimoire and the [**Warlock Toolchain**](https://github.com/Lokee86/warlock-toolchain).
arcana/README.md:6:It models repositories as queryable graphs and provides the storage, snapshot,
arcana/README.md:7:and traversal foundations used by higher-level Warlock tools such as Demon Docs,
arcana/README.md:8:Grimoire, and Pitlord.
arcana/README.md:9:
arcana/README.md:10:## Ownership boundaries
arcana/README.md:11:
arcana/README.md:12:- **Lexicon** owns language parsing and the normalized symbol/relationship fact contract.
arcana/README.md:13:- **Arcana** owns graph ingestion, packed storage, snapshots, deterministic traversal,
arcana/README.md:14:  optional semantic graph indexes, and measurements of storage representations.
arcana/README.md:15:- **Demon Docs** owns documentation semantics, policy, review history, and
arcana/README.md:16:  Codemap decisions. It consumes Arcana facts without owning the graph
arcana/README.md:17:  engine.
arcana/README.md:18:- **Grimoire** owns the provider-neutral discovery interface, source and document
arcana/README.md:19:  retrieval, stable handles, repository-state preparation, and investigation
arcana/README.md:20:  sessions. It queries Arcana without becoming the graph storage layer.
arcana/README.md:21:
arcana/README.md:22:Arcana remains a standalone Rust process or CLI boundary. Go consumers do
arcana/README.md:23:not link it through cgo or FFI.
arcana/README.md:24:
arcana/README.md:25:### Consolidated repository boundary
arcana/README.md:26:
arcana/README.md:27:Arcana and Lexicon now share the Grimoire repository, but the implementation boundary remains intentional. Arcana is still a separate Rust process, independently testable and directly usable for advanced graph work. Lexicon snapshots and the Arcana protocol remain the authoritative integration boundaries; source co-location does not permit direct mutation of Lexicon state or language-analysis ownership.
arcana/README.md:28:
arcana/README.md:29:## Graph workload foundation
arcana/README.md:30:
arcana/README.md:31:Arcana includes deterministic synthetic graph generation for exercising
arcana/README.md:32:its packed storage, snapshot, overlay, and compaction systems across more than a
arcana/README.md:33:single toy topology.
arcana/README.md:34:
arcana/README.md:35:The workload foundation currently includes five topology families:
arcana/README.md:36:
arcana/README.md:37:- **Modular** — cohesive clusters with a configurable cross-cluster edge share.
arcana/README.md:38:- **Entangled** — hubs, cross-cluster relationships, cycles, and local edges.
arcana/README.md:39:- **Hub-heavy** — a small set of nodes owns most incoming and outgoing edges.
arcana/README.md:40:- **Layered** — deep, mostly forward relationships with a smaller irregular
arcana/README.md:41:  edge set.
arcana/README.md:42:- **Dense subsystem** — a tightly connected subsystem inside a larger sparse
arcana/README.md:43:  graph.
arcana/README.md:44:
arcana/README.md:45:Standard scale tiers range from 10,000 nodes and 100,000 edges to 5,000,000
arcana/README.md:46:nodes and 50,000,000 edges. Generation scales with requested edges rather than
arcana/README.md:47:enumerating every possible node pair.
arcana/README.md:48:
arcana/README.md:49:Mutation plans cover single-node, local-range, scattered, hub-focused, and
arcana/README.md:50:percentage updates. A plan contains exact removed and replacement edges so the
arcana/README.md:51:overlay and rebuilt packed snapshot receive the same logical update.
arcana/README.md:52:
arcana/README.md:53:## Determinism and invariants
arcana/README.md:54:
arcana/README.md:55:Synthetic datasets and mutations are controlled by explicit seeds. Generated
arcana/README.md:56:and mutated graphs guarantee:
arcana/README.md:57:
arcana/README.md:58:- exact requested edge counts;
arcana/README.md:59:- unique directed non-self edges;
arcana/README.md:60:- canonical source/target/kind ordering;
arcana/README.md:61:- topology-specific edge distributions;
arcana/README.md:62:- stable output for the same specification and seed; and
arcana/README.md:63:- preserved edge-kind counts across mutations.
arcana/README.md:64:
arcana/README.md:65:The generator uses a small internal permutation sampler and has no third-party
arcana/README.md:66:dependencies. Dataset construction is outside the measured update and query
arcana/README.md:67:windows and is reused by both benchmark paths.
arcana/README.md:68:
arcana/README.md:69:## Packed adjacency format
arcana/README.md:70:
arcana/README.md:71:The immutable packed format uses a fixed, versioned, little-endian header
arcana/README.md:72:followed by aligned forward offsets, forward targets, forward edge kinds,
arcana/README.md:73:reverse offsets, reverse sources, and reverse edge kinds. The writer
arcana/README.md:74:canonicalizes logical edges, streams deterministic bytes through a temporary
arcana/README.md:75:file, syncs them, and atomically commits a new snapshot path.
arcana/README.md:76:
arcana/README.md:77:Opening a packed graph validates the header, exact section layout, file length,
arcana/README.md:78:payload checksum, logical dataset checksum, offset tables, node bounds, and
arcana/README.md:79:adjacency ordering. Queries read directly from the packed byte buffer without
arcana/README.md:80:rebuilding an in-memory graph. A separate in-memory implementation provides the
arcana/README.md:81:correctness oracle used by round-trip tests.
arcana/README.md:82:
arcana/README.md:83:## Snapshots and overlays
arcana/README.md:84:
arcana/README.md:85:Arcana snapshots are immutable compositions rather than mutable graph
arcana/README.md:86:files. A snapshot manifest identifies one validated packed base plus an optional
arcana/README.md:87:immutable overlay. The manifest is published last, so readers never observe a
arcana/README.md:88:partially assembled snapshot.
arcana/README.md:89:
arcana/README.md:90:Overlay v1 stores canonical added edges and removed-edge tombstones bound to the
arcana/README.md:91:exact node count, edge count, and dataset checksum of its packed base. Opening a
arcana/README.md:92:snapshot validates the base, overlay, manifest identities, visible edge count,
arcana/README.md:93:and visible dataset checksum before queries are allowed. Forward and reverse
arcana/README.md:94:queries merge the base adjacency with small in-memory overlay indexes without
arcana/README.md:95:rewriting the packed base.
arcana/README.md:96:
arcana/README.md:97:Snapshot and overlay files are content-identifiable and refuse in-place
arcana/README.md:98:replacement. `compact_snapshot` materializes the visible graph into a new packed
arcana/README.md:99:base, verifies its edge count and checksum, and publishes a new base-only
arcana/README.md:100:manifest last. The source snapshot remains untouched.
arcana/README.md:101:
arcana/README.md:102:## Repository ingestion
arcana/README.md:103:
arcana/README.md:104:Arcana consumes Lexicon's immutable snapshot store, verifies each content-addressed
arcana/README.md:105:fact object, and decodes Lexicon binary v1 node, edge, and unresolved sections
arcana/README.md:106:into typed repository facts without reconstructing JSONL. Legacy canonical JSON
arcana/README.md:107:fact objects remain readable during migration. Language adapters live in the co-located [`../lexicon`](../lexicon/) component; Arcana does not own language parsers.
arcana/README.md:108:
arcana/README.md:109:### Lexicon synchronization
arcana/README.md:110:
arcana/README.md:111:A one-shot sync reads `.lexicon/CURRENT`, verifies the referenced manifest and
arcana/README.md:112:fact objects, and publishes an immutable graph snapshot under `.arcana/`:
arcana/README.md:113:
arcana/README.md:114:```text
arcana/README.md:115:lexicon scan
arcana/README.md:116:arcana sync
arcana/README.md:117:```
arcana/README.md:118:
arcana/README.md:119:Run `arcana sync --register` once to add Arcana as a Lexicon post-publication
arcana/README.md:120:consumer. Every later successful manual or daemon-triggered Lexicon scan then
arcana/README.md:121:invokes the same one-shot Arcana sync command. Arcana compares successive
arcana/README.md:122:Lexicon file-object identities, writes an overlay when the graph node set is
arcana/README.md:123:stable, and rebuilds the packed base when symbols were added or removed or any
arcana/README.md:124:language-level shared fact object changed. Neither process must remain resident
arcana/README.md:125:for this event-driven path.
arcana/README.md:126:
arcana/README.md:127:Each Arcana snapshot records the consumed Lexicon snapshot ID. Arcana serializes
arcana/README.md:128:writers through `.arcana/LOCK` and atomically replaces `.arcana/CURRENT` only
arcana/README.md:129:after the new graph state verifies, so manual and hook-triggered syncs cannot race
arcana/README.md:130:or expose a partial publication.
arcana/README.md:131:
arcana/README.md:132:The compiled output contains:
arcana/README.md:133:
arcana/README.md:134:- `graph.arcana` — packed forward and reverse adjacency;
arcana/README.md:135:- `catalogue.tsv` — dense node IDs mapped back to full Lexicon identities,
arcana/README.md:136:  compact stable keys, paths, names, kinds, content IDs, and source spans;
arcana/README.md:137:- `unresolved.tsv` — unresolved-reference evidence keyed back to catalogue nodes.
arcana/README.md:138:
arcana/README.md:139:```text
arcana/README.md:140:arcana sync --lexicon /path/to/repository/.lexicon \
arcana/README.md:141:  --state /path/to/repository/.arcana
arcana/README.md:142:
arcana/README.md:143:arcana protocol --snapshot \
arcana/README.md:144:  /path/to/repository/.arcana/snapshots/<lexicon-snapshot-digest>
arcana/README.md:145:{"id":"symbol","op":"resolve_symbol","name":"ExampleFunction"}
arcana/README.md:146:{"id":"chain","op":"shortest_call_chain","from_node_id":12,"to_node_id":42}
arcana/README.md:147:{"id":"impact","op":"impact","node_id":42,"max_depth":8}
arcana/README.md:148:{"id":"architecture","op":"architecture_summary","path_prefix":"src","min_community_size":3}
arcana/README.md:149:```
arcana/README.md:150:
arcana/README.md:151:Arcana also reads its legacy TSV fact format during migration. Lexicon SHA-256
arcana/README.md:152:identities remain the durable cross-tool identity; Arcana compacts them into
arcana/README.md:153:snapshot-local packed IDs and rejects any detected compaction collision.
arcana/README.md:154:
arcana/README.md:155:The stable protocol identifier is `arcana.query.v1`. In addition to symbol,
arcana/README.md:156:file, neighbor, unresolved, statistics, and snapshot-diff operations, it supports
arcana/README.md:157:bounded multi-hop paths, entry-point reachability, transitive impact, shortest
arcana/README.md:158:call chains, dead-symbol detection, operational-role summaries, and deterministic
arcana/README.md:159:architecture communities. Architecture summaries can be path-scoped and relation-
arcana/README.md:160:scoped, and report representative nodes, internal relation counts, and incoming or
arcana/README.md:161:outgoing boundary counts.
arcana/README.md:162:
arcana/README.md:163:The repository fact model also accepts `observed-calls`, `routes-to`,
arcana/README.md:164:`communicates-with`, and `similar-to` evidence. Runtime-observed calls participate
arcana/README.md:165:in call traversal and are reported separately from static call resolution.
arcana/README.md:166:
arcana/README.md:167:See [`docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md`](docs/LEXICON_CONTRACT.md) for the exact consumer
arcana/README.md:168:boundary and incremental ownership policy.
arcana/README.md:169:
arcana/README.md:170:## Optional semantic graph index
arcana/README.md:171:
arcana/README.md:172:Arcana can explicitly vectorize the current immutable graph through Grimoire's
arcana/README.md:173:existing OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint. Arcana stores and invalidates the
arcana/README.md:174:graph vectors; it does not install or load a second model. Ordinary `arcana sync`
arcana/README.md:175:and graph-protocol operations remain embedding-free.
arcana/README.md:176:
arcana/README.md:177:```text
arcana/README.md:178:grimoire model serve
arcana/README.md:179:arcana sync
arcana/README.md:180:arcana vectorize
arcana/README.md:181:arcana semantic-query --query "where is profile persistence handled?"
arcana/README.md:182:```
arcana/README.md:183:
arcana/README.md:184:The packed index lives under
arcana/README.md:185:`.arcana/vectors/<snapshot-digest>/<embedding-identity>/`. Immutable graph-document
arcana/README.md:186:vectors live under `.arcana/vector-cache/<embedding-identity>/` and are reused
arcana/README.md:187:across snapshots when rendered content is byte-identical. Successful concurrent
arcana/README.md:188:embedding batches persist immediately, so interrupted builds resume without
arcana/README.md:189:repeating completed work. Each vector represents an eligible declaration-level
arcana/README.md:190:graph entry point plus a bounded immediate neighborhood. Variables, parameters,
arcana/README.md:191:fields, imports, exports, directories, and repository roots remain in the complete
arcana/README.md:192:graph but are not indexed directly. Semantic matches provide entry points; exact
arcana/README.md:193:Arcana traversal remains authoritative for relationships, impact, and call chains.
arcana/README.md:194:
arcana/README.md:195:The semantic index is currently consumed by Arcana's standalone `semantic-query`
arcana/README.md:196:command and paired Arcana evaluation. Grimoire's unified discovery interface uses
arcana/README.md:197:deterministic Lexicon symbol resolution and Arcana graph queries; it does not
arcana/README.md:198:silently build or require the semantic index.
arcana/README.md:199:
arcana/README.md:200:See [`docs/vector-index.md`](docs/vector-index.md) for storage, invalidation,
arcana/README.md:201:commands, and integration details.
arcana/README.md:202:
arcana/README.md:203:## Benchmarks
arcana/README.md:204:
arcana/README.md:205:The benchmark harness compares immutable overlays against rebuilding a complete
arcana/README.md:206:packed replacement while treating the existing packed base as shared storage:
arcana/README.md:207:
arcana/README.md:208:```text
arcana/README.md:209:cargo run --release -- benchmark \
arcana/README.md:210:  --tier small \
arcana/README.md:211:  --topology modular \
arcana/README.md:212:  --queries 10000 \
arcana/README.md:213:  --samples 3 \
arcana/README.md:214:  --csv target/benchmarks/small-modular-mutations.csv
arcana/README.md:215:```
arcana/README.md:216:
arcana/README.md:217:Supported tiers are `small`, `medium`, `large`, and `stress`. Supported
arcana/README.md:218:synthetic topologies are `modular`, `entangled`, `hub-heavy`, `layered`, and
arcana/README.md:219:`dense-subsystem`.
arcana/README.md:220:
arcana/README.md:221:The five mutation workloads cover one hot node, a local range, scattered
arcana/README.md:222:changes, hub-focused changes, and one percent of all edges. Each run measures
arcana/README.md:223:creation, fully validated reopen, warm forward/reverse queries, and incremental
arcana/README.md:224:file size. Overlay and rebuilt-packed results must produce identical visible
arcana/README.md:225:graph checksums and query fingerprints.
arcana/README.md:226:
arcana/README.md:227:## Development
arcana/README.md:228:
arcana/README.md:229:The package uses Rust edition 2024.
arcana/README.md:230:
arcana/README.md:231:```text
arcana/README.md:232:cargo fmt -- --check
arcana/README.md:233:cargo check --all-targets
arcana/README.md:234:cargo test --all-targets
arcana/README.md:235:cargo run -- --help
arcana/README.md:236:cargo run -- --version
arcana/README.md:237:```
arcana/README.md:238:
arcana/README.md:239:## License
arcana/README.md:240:
arcana/README.md:241:Arcana is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE.md).
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:1:# Lexicon application
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:2:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:3:Lexicon keeps the most recently observed relevant repository state. It does not follow the source repository's commits, index, staging area, or branches.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:4:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:5:## Runtime model
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:6:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:7:Lexicon is primarily a one-shot CLI. `init`, `scan`, `rebuild`, `languages set`, `export`, `gc`, `consumer`, `status`, and `doctor` perform bounded operations and exit.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:8:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:9:`lexicon demon` is an optional watch mode. It remains active only to translate filesystem events and periodic reconciliation into the same locked scan transaction used by `lexicon scan`. Snapshot consumers do not depend on the watch process and can read any published snapshot after Lexicon exits.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:10:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:11:When `--repo` is omitted, initialized commands walk upward from the current directory until they find `.lexicon/config.json`. `lexicon init` uses an already initialized ancestor when present; otherwise it initializes the current directory. An explicit `--repo` always selects that directory directly.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:12:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:13:## Concurrency
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:14:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:15:A scan may execute independent language plans concurrently. A weighted scheduler limits their combined reserved work to the process-wide `GOMAXPROCS` CPU budget.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:16:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:17:The Go adapter also receives repository-size-dependent logical shard, active worker, and merge fan-in values. Typed call and dataflow work executes in shard-local scanners, merges through a deterministic reduction tree, and is followed by repository-wide SSA/VTA resolution. Logical shard count is independent from active worker count. `LEXICON_MAX_WORKERS` may lower the worker ceiling for constrained machines or CI.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:18:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:19:Concurrency must not change output. Identical source, adapter versions, schema, and analysis configuration must produce byte-identical facts regardless of valid worker count or merge shape.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:20:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:21:## Post-publication consumers
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:22:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:23:Lexicon can invoke deterministic one-shot consumers after a successful scan has published or confirmed the current immutable snapshot. Consumer definitions live under `.lexicon/consumers/*.json`:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:24:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:25:```json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:26:{
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:27:  "version": 1,
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:28:  "command": "/absolute/path/to/arcana",
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:29:  "args": ["sync", "--lexicon", "/repo/.lexicon", "--state", "/repo/.arcana"],
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:30:  "timeout": "30s"
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:31:}
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:32:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:33:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:34:Commands execute directly without a shell, in lexical filename order, with the repository as their working directory. `timeout` is optional; existing definitions without it remain unlimited. Lexicon provides `LEXICON_REPOSITORY`, `LEXICON_STATE_ROOT`, and `LEXICON_SNAPSHOT_ID`. Lexicon attempts every registered consumer, aggregates failures, and retries failed consumers on a later scan. After a successful invocation, its state file contains deterministic JSON such as `{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"sha256:..."}` and is replaced atomically; failed invocations leave their previous state unchanged. The already-published Lexicon snapshot remains valid.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:35:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:36:The `lexicon consumer` commands and `internal/consumer` package expose list, add, remove, and one-shot execution operations. Definition names are simple `.json` filenames; path traversal and other extensions are rejected. Listing is lexical, adding replaces an existing definition atomically, removal deletes both the definition and its consumer state, and one-shot execution validates the requested immutable snapshot before invoking the selected consumer.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:37:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:38:## Commands
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:39:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:40:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:41:lexicon init [--repo PATH] [--adapters PATH] [--languages all|LIST]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:42:lexicon scan [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:43:lexicon demon [--repo PATH] [--debounce 150ms] [--reconcile 30s]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:44:lexicon rebuild [--repo PATH] [--languages LIST]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:45:lexicon languages [list] [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:46:lexicon languages set [--repo PATH] --languages all|LIST
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:47:lexicon status [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:48:lexicon doctor [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:49:lexicon export [--repo PATH] --output PATH [--snapshot ID] [--languages LIST]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:50:lexicon gc [--repo PATH] [--retain 20] [--dry-run]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:51:lexicon consumer list [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:52:lexicon consumer add [--repo PATH] --name NAME --command PATH [--arg VALUE]... [--timeout DURATION]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:53:lexicon consumer remove [--repo PATH] --name NAME
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:54:lexicon consumer run [--repo PATH] --name NAME [--snapshot ID]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:55:lexicon version
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:56:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:57:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:58:`lexicon init` creates `.lexicon/repo`, performs complete analysis for the selected detected languages, creates the initial private state commit, and publishes an immutable analysis snapshot. Omitting `--languages` or using `all` enables every supported language.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:59:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:60:`lexicon scan` replaces the private source mirror with the repository's current relevant files. The private Git repository supplies the diff from the last successful scan. For ordinary source-file modifications, Lexicon expands changed paths through the previous snapshot's reverse dependency graph, requests incremental JSONL records for that impacted file set, parses the stream once at the adapter boundary, writes replacement per-file objects, reuses every unaffected manifest entry, and publishes a new immutable snapshot. Structural changes and adapter fingerprint changes use complete-language analysis.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:61:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:62:`lexicon demon` watches the repository recursively and invokes the same scan transaction after a debounce. A periodic complete reconciliation repairs missed filesystem events.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:63:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:64:`lexicon rebuild` forces complete analysis of all enabled detected languages or an explicit enabled subset. `lexicon languages set` updates the configured selection, removes disabled language entries from the snapshot, scans immediately, and publishes the result.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:65:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:66:`lexicon status` reports the repository, current snapshot, detected and enabled languages, and consumers. `lexicon doctor` verifies configuration, private Git state, immutable objects, adapter paths, runtime requirements, and consumer commands.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:67:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:68:`lexicon export` reconstructs verified standalone JSONL libraries. `lexicon gc` deletes only unreachable snapshots and objects while preserving retention and consumer pins. Consumer commands manage and invoke deterministic post-publication hooks.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:69:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:70:## Private state repository
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:71:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:72:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:73:.lexicon/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:74:    config.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:75:    CURRENT
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:76:    LOCK
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:77:    PENDING              # transient crash-recovery record
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:78:    consumers/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:79:        arcana.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:80:    consumer-state/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:81:        arcana.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:82:    objects/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:83:        ab/cdef...
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:84:    snapshots/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:85:        <snapshot-id>.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:86:    repo/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:87:        .git/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:88:        source/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:89:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:90:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:91:The state commit is always amended and remains a parentless root commit, so only one commit is reachable. Reflogs are expired after replacement. The repository is an implementation detail used to answer one question: what source content changed since Lexicon last successfully published a snapshot?
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:92:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:93:Each snapshot manifest records the internal state commit, adapter and schema versions, configuration identity, source-content identity, and fact-object identity for every relevant file. Shared synthetic facts are stored in a separate language object. Objects and snapshot manifests are immutable; identical content reuses the existing object. Fact objects use Lexicon's deterministic binary v1 codec with a shared string table and independently length-prefixed node, edge, and unresolved sections. JSONL is reconstructed only by `lexicon export`; snapshot consumers can skip unused binary sections and attributes.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:94:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:95:`CURRENT` contains the complete snapshot ID and is replaced atomically only after the internal state commit and every referenced object are durable. Consumers should resolve `CURRENT`, load the corresponding manifest, and then open its objects. They never need to observe the mutable mirror or adapter JSONL transport files.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:96:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:97:## Object garbage collection
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:98:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:99:Objectstore garbage collection retains the snapshot named by `CURRENT` and the configured number of newest snapshot manifests. It also retains every snapshot named by a `snapshot_id` field in `.lexicon/consumer-state/*.json`; those pins protect consumer work that still refers to an older immutable snapshot. A pinned snapshot that is missing, or a pin file that is malformed or lacks a valid `snapshot_id`, is a hard error and aborts collection.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:100:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:101:The planner follows every preserved manifest's file and shared-object references. Execution deletes only unreferenced snapshot manifests and fact objects. Planning and deletion are deterministic, and execution rejects a plan if `CURRENT` changed after planning. `Store.GarbageCollect(options, dryRun)` performs the bounded plan-and-execute transaction; `dryRun` returns the same deletion lists without removing any files. The explicit planning and execution methods remain available when callers need to inspect a plan before applying it.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:102:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:103:## Snapshot export
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:104:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:105:The `lexicon export` command and objectstore export API write standalone language libraries without changing the current snapshot:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:106:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:107:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:108:lexicon export --output /tmp/lexicon-export --languages python,go
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:109:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:110:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:111:```go
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:112:err := (objectstore.Store{Root: "/repo/.lexicon"}).Export(
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:113:    "CURRENT", "/tmp/lexicon-export", []string{"python", "go"},
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:114:)
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:115:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:116:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:117:The snapshot argument may be `CURRENT`, an exact snapshot ID, or empty (which
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:118:also resolves `CURRENT`). An empty language list exports every language;
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:119:requested languages must exist in the manifest. Each selected language becomes
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:120:`<language>.jsonl` in the destination. Export reconstructs the full header from
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:121:manifest metadata, verifies every referenced object, combines shared and
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:122:per-file records, sorts records deterministically, and atomically replaces each
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:123:destination file.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:124:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:125:## Transaction and recovery
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:126:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:127:Only one process may update a repository at a time. Manual scans and demon updates acquire the same advisory lock; a competing writer receives an explicit busy error.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:128:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:129:Before advancing the private state commit, Lexicon writes a durable `PENDING` record containing the complete candidate manifest and whether the source commit must advance. If a process stops before the commit, the next scan discards that candidate and recomputes it. If the commit succeeded but publication did not, the next scan attaches the committed state ID to the pending manifest and atomically publishes it without rerunning adapters. Publications that do not require a source commit, such as adapter-only rebuilds, are also recoverable from `PENDING`.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:130:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:131:Existing installations that still contain committed `.lexicon/repo/library/*.jsonl` files are migrated once into snapshot objects when necessary, after which the materialized directory is removed from the private state commit. New scans never create it.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:132:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:133:## Incremental boundary
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:134:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:135:A modified source file starts an impacted-file object update rather than a complete language rewrite. Lexicon reads the previous immutable snapshot, follows cross-file edges in reverse, and includes every transitive dependent. Files that previously contained unresolved relationships are also included conservatively because a newly introduced declaration may resolve them.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:136:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:137:Lexicon builds a temporary scoped repository containing the impacted files, their transitive forward dependencies from the previous snapshot, and the language's configuration files. Go scopes expand to complete packages and Rust scopes expand to complete crates because those are their minimum sound semantic units. The adapter emits only records owned by the impacted files. Shared synthetic records from the scoped view are marked partial and are not allowed to replace the previous complete shared set.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:138:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:139:A directly edited file that already owns cross-file or unresolved relationships uses complete-language analysis immediately, because a partial candidate universe could preserve the same edge identity while changing its true resolution. Leaf and local-only files use the scoped path. Before applying a scoped result, Lexicon compares emitted edge and unresolved topology with the previous file objects. A new relationship, a new unresolved reference, or a scoped adapter failure automatically retries the complete language repository. When the scoped result is accepted, unaffected file objects remain byte-identical and are reused.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:140:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:141:Additions, deletions, renames, copies, language configuration changes, missing prior dependency data, and invalid prior snapshot state trigger a complete rebuild of the affected language. This is a correctness boundary, not a permanent protocol limitation. The incremental contract already carries removed-file scopes, so future dependency metadata can narrow those cases without changing consumers or snapshot storage.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:142:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:143:## Watch behavior
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:144:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:145:The demon ignores Git metadata, Lexicon state, linked worktrees, dependency directories, and build outputs. An optional repository-root `.lexiconignore` adds gitignore-compatible patterns, including comments, globs, `**`, path hierarchy, and `!` negation, on top of those permanent exclusions. Ignored files are omitted from complete mirror scans, path syncs, and demon watch filtering. Permanent exclusions cannot be re-included by `.lexiconignore`; they include `.git/`, `.worktrees/`, `.workingtrees/`, the Warlock state directories, `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `target/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `__pycache__/`, and `.pytest_cache/`.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:146:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:147:The demon keeps the loaded ignore policy in memory while processing filesystem events. A change to `.lexiconignore` reloads the policy, refreshes recursive watches, and triggers a complete scan. New directories are watched recursively. Deletes and renames remove their mirrored paths. Watcher errors trigger an immediate full reconciliation, and the configured reconciliation interval provides an additional recovery path.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1:# Lexicon architecture
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:3:Lexicon is an on-demand repository analysis application with an optional watch mode. It owns language extraction, normalized facts, incremental analysis decisions, immutable fact storage, and atomic snapshot publication.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:4:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:5:It is not a general graph database, retrieval engine, documentation manager, or version-control system.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:6:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:7:## Ownership boundaries
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:8:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:9:### Lexicon owns
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:10:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11:- one reusable semantic adapter per supported language surface;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:12:- stable cross-tool node identities and normalized relationship vocabulary;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:13:- source spans, provenance, file ownership, and unresolved evidence;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:14:- complete and incremental adapter execution;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:15:- content-addressed per-file and shared-language fact objects;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16:- immutable snapshot manifests and the `CURRENT` publication pointer;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:17:- post-publication consumer registration and invocation;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:18:- deterministic export back to facts-v1 JSONL;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:19:- repository-wide cross-stack contract resolution over adapter facts and source evidence.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:20:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21:### Lexicon does not own
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:22:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:23:- packed graph query execution, reachability, impact analysis, or graph traversal;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:24:- lexical or vector retrieval and context-package construction;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:25:- documentation policy or automated documentation repair;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:26:- runtime instrumentation providers;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:27:- source-repository history or branch management.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:28:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:29:Arcana may consume Lexicon snapshots, but Lexicon remains independently executable and does not require Arcana.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:30:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:31:## Component map
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:32:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:33:```text
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:34:cmd/lexicon
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:35:    -> internal/cli
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:36:        -> internal/scan
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:37:            -> internal/files and internal/state
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:38:            -> internal/scope
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:39:            -> internal/adapters
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:40:            -> internal/objectstore
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:41:            -> internal/interstack
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:42:            -> internal/consumer
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:43:        -> internal/watch
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:44:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:45:adapters/<language>
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:46:    -> facts-v1 JSONL
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:47:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:48:.lexicon/
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:49:    -> immutable objects and manifests
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:50:    -> CURRENT publication pointer
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:51:```
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:53:### CLI
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:55:`cmd/lexicon` delegates command behavior to `internal/cli`. The CLI resolves a repository, loads its configuration, and invokes one bounded operation. `lexicon demon` is the exception: it remains active only to convert filesystem events into the same scan transaction used by `lexicon scan`.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:56:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:57:### Repository state and file discovery
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:58:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:59:`internal/files` defines relevant source discovery and permanent exclusions. `.lexiconignore` adds repository-specific gitignore-compatible exclusions but cannot re-include permanent state, dependency, or build directories.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:60:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:61:`internal/state` maintains a private source mirror beneath `.lexicon/repo`. Its Git repository is a change detector between successful Lexicon publications. It is deliberately not a second user-facing source history.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:62:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:63:### Adapter orchestration
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:64:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:65:`internal/adapters` locates and invokes the self-contained language adapters. Adapters receive a repository root, output path, optional changed and removed file scopes, and optional parallel-execution parameters. They emit one deterministic facts-v1 JSONL stream.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:66:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:67:Adapters do not write Lexicon snapshots directly and do not contain consumer-specific graph or retrieval policy.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:68:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69:### Cross-stack resolution
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:70:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:71:`internal/interstack` runs after the selected language adapters have produced a complete candidate manifest. It consumes their immutable facts, maps framework and transport declarations back to existing language-owned nodes, and emits one synthetic `interstack` facts library.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:72:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:73:The initial resolver covers HTTP requests and routes, packet/message producers and consumers, and shared environment/configuration keys. Its synthetic nodes are contracts, not replacements for language symbols. Cross-stack edges retain source evidence, confidence, and unresolved outcomes rather than converting ambiguous string matches into definite graph relationships.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:74:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:75:Arcana stores and traverses these relationships. Lexicon owns discovering them because route DSLs, packet construction, handler registration, and configuration access require source- and framework-aware analysis.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:76:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:77:### Analysis planning
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:78:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:79:`internal/scan` compares the current relevant source tree with the last successfully published source state. It selects either:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:80:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:81:- complete-language analysis; or
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:82:- a scoped analysis containing impacted owners, required dependency context, and language configuration files.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:83:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:84:The planner treats correctness as the priority. Structural changes, invalid prior state, unsupported ownership, unsafe topology changes, or scoped adapter failure trigger complete-language analysis.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:85:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:86:### Object storage
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:87:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:88:`internal/objectstore` parses validated adapter output and partitions records into:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:89:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:90:- one immutable object per owned source file; and
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:91:- an optional shared object for unowned synthetic language facts.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:92:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:93:New objects use the deterministic binary format in `spec/objects-v1.md`. Object identity is content-addressed. Existing bytes under an object ID are immutable.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:94:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:95:A snapshot manifest references every object required for one complete repository analysis state. `CURRENT` is replaced atomically only after all referenced objects and the manifest are durable.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:96:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:97:### Consumers
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:98:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:99:`internal/consumer` manages deterministic one-shot consumers registered under `.lexicon/consumers/`. Consumers run after successful publication or confirmation of the current snapshot. A consumer failure does not invalidate the already-published Lexicon snapshot.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:100:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:101:Consumers receive the repository, state root, and snapshot ID through environment variables and should read only the immutable manifest and objects referenced by that snapshot.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:102:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:103:## Analysis lifecycle
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:104:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:105:A normal scan performs this sequence:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:106:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:107:1. resolve the initialized repository and acquire the repository update lock;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:108:2. load configuration, the current manifest, and any recoverable pending publication;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:109:3. mirror the current relevant source tree;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:110:4. calculate changed, added, deleted, renamed, and configuration paths;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:111:5. determine affected languages and safe complete or scoped plans;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:112:6. execute adapters under the resource scheduler;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:113:7. validate and parse each facts-v1 stream once;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:114:8. build replacement owned objects and reuse unaffected manifest entries;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:115:9. derive the synthetic repository-wide `interstack` library from the candidate language facts;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:116:10. write missing immutable objects;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:117:11. write the durable `PENDING` candidate;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:118:12. advance the private source-state commit when required;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:119:13. write the immutable snapshot manifest;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:120:14. atomically replace `CURRENT` and remove `PENDING`;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:121:15. invoke registered consumers;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:122:16. release the lock.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:123:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:124:A scan that produces the same complete manifest confirms the existing snapshot instead of publishing duplicate mutable state.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:125:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:126:## Incremental correctness boundary
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:127:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:128:A changed source file does not automatically imply a full language scan. Lexicon starts from the previous immutable snapshot and follows cross-file relationships in reverse to identify transitive dependents. Owners with unresolved relationships are included conservatively.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:129:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:130:The scoped repository includes:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:131:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:132:- impacted owners;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:133:- their required forward dependency context;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:134:- language configuration files;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:135:- complete packages for Go;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:136:- complete crates for Rust.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:137:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:138:A scoped stream may replace only facts owned by its declared changed files. Partial shared facts cannot replace the previous complete shared object.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:139:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:140:Lexicon retries with complete-language analysis when:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:141:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:142:- a direct edit previously owned cross-file or unresolved relationships;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:143:- the scoped result introduces relationship or unresolved topology that cannot be proven safe;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:144:- an adapter emits the wrong stream mode;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:145:- scoped execution fails;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:146:- additions, deletions, renames, copies, configuration changes, or invalid prior state make ownership uncertain.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:147:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:148:This fallback is part of the correctness design, not an error condition.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:149:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:150:## Concurrency model
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:151:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:152:Full scans may run independent language plans concurrently. A weighted scheduler limits their combined reserved CPU weight to the process-wide `GOMAXPROCS` budget.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:153:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:154:The Go adapter has a second level of parallelism:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:155:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:156:1. Lexicon inventories Go source count and bytes.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:157:2. It selects a repository-size-dependent logical shard count.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:158:3. It chooses a bounded active worker count.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:159:4. Typed call and dataflow work executes in shard-local scanners.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:160:5. Results merge through a deterministic fan-in reduction tree.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:161:6. Repository-wide SSA/VTA resolution runs after the typed shard merge.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:162:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:163:Logical shards are work partitions, not simultaneous workers. The planner may create many logical shards while activating only a bounded number of workers. `LEXICON_MAX_WORKERS` can lower the active-worker ceiling.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:164:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:165:All supported worker counts and merge shapes must produce byte-identical facts.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:166:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:167:## Multi-module Go ownership
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:168:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:169:The Go adapter discovers every `go.mod` beneath the scanned repository, assigns each Go source file to its nearest module root, and analyzes modules independently before deterministic fact merge. Repository identity is the root module path when a root module exists; otherwise it is the repository directory name.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:170:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:171:Package and symbol identities remain module-qualified. Nested modules do not inherit the parent module path.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:172:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:173:## Publication and recovery
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:174:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:175:`PENDING` records the complete candidate manifest before mutable source-state advancement. Recovery distinguishes three cases:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:176:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:177:- source state did not advance: discard the candidate and recompute;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:178:- source state advanced but publication did not: attach the committed state and publish without rerunning adapters;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:179:- publication requires no source-state change: publish the durable candidate directly.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:180:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:181:Consumers resolve `CURRENT` once and then read immutable data. They observe either the previous complete snapshot or the new complete snapshot, never a partially written analysis state.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:182:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:183:## Compatibility boundaries
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:184:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:185:The public compatibility surfaces are the versioned contracts under `spec/`, the CLI behavior documented in `docs/APPLICATION.md`, and the consumer definition format.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:186:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:187:Internal package structure, temporary adapter JSONL paths, private mirror implementation, scheduling heuristics, and binary storage implementation details outside the versioned object contract may change without becoming public application APIs.
