lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1:# Lexicon architecture
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:3:Lexicon is an on-demand repository analysis application with an optional watch mode. It owns language extraction, normalized facts, incremental analysis decisions, immutable fact storage, and atomic snapshot publication.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:4:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:5:It is not a general graph database, retrieval engine, documentation manager, or version-control system.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:6:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:7:## Ownership boundaries
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:8:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:9:### Lexicon owns
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:10:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11:- one reusable semantic adapter per supported language surface;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:12:- stable cross-tool node identities and normalized relationship vocabulary;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:13:- source spans, provenance, file ownership, and unresolved evidence;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:14:- complete and incremental adapter execution;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:15:- content-addressed per-file and shared-language fact objects;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16:- immutable snapshot manifests and the `CURRENT` publication pointer;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:17:- post-publication consumer registration and invocation;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:18:- deterministic export back to facts-v1 JSONL;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:19:- repository-wide cross-stack contract resolution over adapter facts and source evidence.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:20:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21:### Lexicon does not own
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:22:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:23:- packed graph query execution, reachability, impact analysis, or graph traversal;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:24:- lexical or vector retrieval and context-package construction;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:25:- documentation policy or automated documentation repair;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:26:- runtime instrumentation providers;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:27:- source-repository history or branch management.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:28:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:29:Arcana may consume Lexicon snapshots, but Lexicon remains independently executable and does not require Arcana.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:30:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:31:## Component map
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:32:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:33:```text
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:34:cmd/lexicon
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:35:    -> internal/cli
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:36:        -> internal/scan
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:37:            -> internal/files and internal/state
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:38:            -> internal/scope
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:39:            -> internal/adapters
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:40:            -> internal/objectstore
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:41:            -> internal/interstack
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:42:            -> internal/consumer
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:43:        -> internal/watch
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:44:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:45:adapters/<language>
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:46:    -> facts-v1 JSONL
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:47:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:48:.lexicon/
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:49:    -> immutable objects and manifests
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:50:    -> CURRENT publication pointer
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:51:```
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:53:### CLI
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:55:`cmd/lexicon` delegates command behavior to `internal/cli`. The CLI resolves a repository, loads its configuration, and invokes one bounded operation. `lexicon demon` is the exception: it remains active only to convert filesystem events into the same scan transaction used by `lexicon scan`.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:56:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:57:### Repository state and file discovery
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:58:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:59:`internal/files` defines relevant source discovery and permanent exclusions. `.lexiconignore` adds repository-specific gitignore-compatible exclusions but cannot re-include permanent state, dependency, or build directories.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:60:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:61:`internal/state` maintains a private source mirror beneath `.lexicon/repo`. Its Git repository is a change detector between successful Lexicon publications. It is deliberately not a second user-facing source history.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:62:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:63:### Adapter orchestration
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:64:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:65:`internal/adapters` locates and invokes the self-contained language adapters. Adapters receive a repository root, output path, optional changed and removed file scopes, and optional parallel-execution parameters. They emit one deterministic facts-v1 JSONL stream.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:66:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:67:Adapters do not write Lexicon snapshots directly and do not contain consumer-specific graph or retrieval policy.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:68:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69:### Cross-stack resolution
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:70:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:71:`internal/interstack` runs after the selected language adapters have produced a complete candidate manifest. It consumes their immutable facts, maps framework and transport declarations back to existing language-owned nodes, and emits one synthetic `interstack` facts library.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:72:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:73:The initial resolver covers HTTP requests and routes, packet/message producers and consumers, and shared environment/configuration keys. Its synthetic nodes are contracts, not replacements for language symbols. Cross-stack edges retain source evidence, confidence, and unresolved outcomes rather than converting ambiguous string matches into definite graph relationships.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:74:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:75:Arcana stores and traverses these relationships. Lexicon owns discovering them because route DSLs, packet construction, handler registration, and configuration access require source- and framework-aware analysis.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:76:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:77:### Analysis planning
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:78:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:79:`internal/scan` compares the current relevant source tree with the last successfully published source state. It selects either:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:80:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:81:- complete-language analysis; or
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:82:- a scoped analysis containing impacted owners, required dependency context, and language configuration files.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:83:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:84:The planner treats correctness as the priority. Structural changes, invalid prior state, unsupported ownership, unsafe topology changes, or scoped adapter failure trigger complete-language analysis.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:85:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:86:### Object storage
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:87:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:88:`internal/objectstore` parses validated adapter output and partitions records into:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:89:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:90:- one immutable object per owned source file; and
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:91:- an optional shared object for unowned synthetic language facts.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:92:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:93:New objects use the deterministic binary format in `spec/objects-v1.md`. Object identity is content-addressed. Existing bytes under an object ID are immutable.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:94:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:95:A snapshot manifest references every object required for one complete repository analysis state. `CURRENT` is replaced atomically only after all referenced objects and the manifest are durable.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:96:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:97:### Consumers
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:98:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:99:`internal/consumer` manages deterministic one-shot consumers registered under `.lexicon/consumers/`. Consumers run after successful publication or confirmation of the current snapshot. A consumer failure does not invalidate the already-published Lexicon snapshot.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:100:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:101:Consumers receive the repository, state root, and snapshot ID through environment variables and should read only the immutable manifest and objects referenced by that snapshot.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:102:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:103:## Analysis lifecycle
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:104:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:105:A normal scan performs this sequence:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:106:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:107:1. resolve the initialized repository and acquire the repository update lock;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:108:2. load configuration, the current manifest, and any recoverable pending publication;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:109:3. mirror the current relevant source tree;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:110:4. calculate changed, added, deleted, renamed, and configuration paths;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:111:5. determine affected languages and safe complete or scoped plans;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:112:6. execute adapters under the resource scheduler;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:113:7. validate and parse each facts-v1 stream once;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:114:8. build replacement owned objects and reuse unaffected manifest entries;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:115:9. derive the synthetic repository-wide `interstack` library from the candidate language facts;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:116:10. write missing immutable objects;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:117:11. write the durable `PENDING` candidate;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:118:12. advance the private source-state commit when required;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:119:13. write the immutable snapshot manifest;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:120:14. atomically replace `CURRENT` and remove `PENDING`;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:121:15. invoke registered consumers;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:122:16. release the lock.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:123:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:124:A scan that produces the same complete manifest confirms the existing snapshot instead of publishing duplicate mutable state.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:125:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:126:## Incremental correctness boundary
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:127:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:128:A changed source file does not automatically imply a full language scan. Lexicon starts from the previous immutable snapshot and follows cross-file relationships in reverse to identify transitive dependents. Owners with unresolved relationships are included conservatively.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:129:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:130:The scoped repository includes:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:131:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:132:- impacted owners;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:133:- their required forward dependency context;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:134:- language configuration files;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:135:- complete packages for Go;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:136:- complete crates for Rust.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:137:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:138:A scoped stream may replace only facts owned by its declared changed files. Partial shared facts cannot replace the previous complete shared object.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:139:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:140:Lexicon retries with complete-language analysis when:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:141:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:142:- a direct edit previously owned cross-file or unresolved relationships;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:143:- the scoped result introduces relationship or unresolved topology that cannot be proven safe;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:144:- an adapter emits the wrong stream mode;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:145:- scoped execution fails;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:146:- additions, deletions, renames, copies, configuration changes, or invalid prior state make ownership uncertain.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:147:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:148:This fallback is part of the correctness design, not an error condition.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:149:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:150:## Concurrency model
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:151:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:152:Full scans may run independent language plans concurrently. A weighted scheduler limits their combined reserved CPU weight to the process-wide `GOMAXPROCS` budget.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:153:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:154:The Go adapter has a second level of parallelism:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:155:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:156:1. Lexicon inventories Go source count and bytes.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:157:2. It selects a repository-size-dependent logical shard count.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:158:3. It chooses a bounded active worker count.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:159:4. Typed call and dataflow work executes in shard-local scanners.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:160:5. Results merge through a deterministic fan-in reduction tree.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:161:6. Repository-wide SSA/VTA resolution runs after the typed shard merge.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:162:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:163:Logical shards are work partitions, not simultaneous workers. The planner may create many logical shards while activating only a bounded number of workers. `LEXICON_MAX_WORKERS` can lower the active-worker ceiling.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:164:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:165:All supported worker counts and merge shapes must produce byte-identical facts.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:166:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:167:## Multi-module Go ownership
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:168:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:169:The Go adapter discovers every `go.mod` beneath the scanned repository, assigns each Go source file to its nearest module root, and analyzes modules independently before deterministic fact merge. Repository identity is the root module path when a root module exists; otherwise it is the repository directory name.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:170:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:171:Package and symbol identities remain module-qualified. Nested modules do not inherit the parent module path.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:172:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:173:## Publication and recovery
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:174:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:175:`PENDING` records the complete candidate manifest before mutable source-state advancement. Recovery distinguishes three cases:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:176:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:177:- source state did not advance: discard the candidate and recompute;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:178:- source state advanced but publication did not: attach the committed state and publish without rerunning adapters;
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:179:- publication requires no source-state change: publish the durable candidate directly.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:180:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:181:Consumers resolve `CURRENT` once and then read immutable data. They observe either the previous complete snapshot or the new complete snapshot, never a partially written analysis state.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:182:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:183:## Compatibility boundaries
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:184:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:185:The public compatibility surfaces are the versioned contracts under `spec/`, the CLI behavior documented in `docs/APPLICATION.md`, and the consumer definition format.
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:186:
lexicon/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:187:Internal package structure, temporary adapter JSONL paths, private mirror implementation, scheduling heuristics, and binary storage implementation details outside the versioned object contract may change without becoming public application APIs.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:1:# Lexicon application
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:2:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:3:Lexicon keeps the most recently observed relevant repository state. It does not follow the source repository's commits, index, staging area, or branches.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:4:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:5:## Runtime model
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:6:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:7:Lexicon is primarily a one-shot CLI. `init`, `scan`, `rebuild`, `languages set`, `export`, `gc`, `consumer`, `status`, and `doctor` perform bounded operations and exit.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:8:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:9:`lexicon demon` is an optional watch mode. It remains active only to translate filesystem events and periodic reconciliation into the same locked scan transaction used by `lexicon scan`. Snapshot consumers do not depend on the watch process and can read any published snapshot after Lexicon exits.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:10:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:11:When `--repo` is omitted, initialized commands walk upward from the current directory until they find `.lexicon/config.json`. `lexicon init` uses an already initialized ancestor when present; otherwise it initializes the current directory. An explicit `--repo` always selects that directory directly.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:12:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:13:## Concurrency
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:14:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:15:A scan may execute independent language plans concurrently. A weighted scheduler limits their combined reserved work to the process-wide `GOMAXPROCS` CPU budget.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:16:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:17:The Go adapter also receives repository-size-dependent logical shard, active worker, and merge fan-in values. Typed call and dataflow work executes in shard-local scanners, merges through a deterministic reduction tree, and is followed by repository-wide SSA/VTA resolution. Logical shard count is independent from active worker count. `LEXICON_MAX_WORKERS` may lower the worker ceiling for constrained machines or CI.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:18:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:19:Concurrency must not change output. Identical source, adapter versions, schema, and analysis configuration must produce byte-identical facts regardless of valid worker count or merge shape.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:20:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:21:## Post-publication consumers
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:22:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:23:Lexicon can invoke deterministic one-shot consumers after a successful scan has published or confirmed the current immutable snapshot. Consumer definitions live under `.lexicon/consumers/*.json`:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:24:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:25:```json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:26:{
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:27:  "version": 1,
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:28:  "command": "/absolute/path/to/arcana",
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:29:  "args": ["sync", "--lexicon", "/repo/.lexicon", "--state", "/repo/.arcana"],
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:30:  "timeout": "30s"
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:31:}
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:32:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:33:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:34:Commands execute directly without a shell, in lexical filename order, with the repository as their working directory. `timeout` is optional; existing definitions without it remain unlimited. Lexicon provides `LEXICON_REPOSITORY`, `LEXICON_STATE_ROOT`, and `LEXICON_SNAPSHOT_ID`. Lexicon attempts every registered consumer, aggregates failures, and retries failed consumers on a later scan. After a successful invocation, its state file contains deterministic JSON such as `{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"sha256:..."}` and is replaced atomically; failed invocations leave their previous state unchanged. The already-published Lexicon snapshot remains valid.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:35:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:36:The `lexicon consumer` commands and `internal/consumer` package expose list, add, remove, and one-shot execution operations. Definition names are simple `.json` filenames; path traversal and other extensions are rejected. Listing is lexical, adding replaces an existing definition atomically, removal deletes both the definition and its consumer state, and one-shot execution validates the requested immutable snapshot before invoking the selected consumer.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:37:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:38:## Commands
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:39:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:40:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:41:lexicon init [--repo PATH] [--adapters PATH] [--languages all|LIST]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:42:lexicon scan [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:43:lexicon demon [--repo PATH] [--debounce 150ms] [--reconcile 30s]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:44:lexicon rebuild [--repo PATH] [--languages LIST]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:45:lexicon languages [list] [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:46:lexicon languages set [--repo PATH] --languages all|LIST
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:47:lexicon status [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:48:lexicon doctor [--repo PATH]
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:49:lexicon export [--repo PATH] --output PATH [--snapshot ID] [--languages LIST]

lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:58:`lexicon init` creates `.lexicon/repo`, performs complete analysis for the selected detected languages, creates the initial private state commit, and publishes an immutable analysis snapshot. Omitting `--languages` or using `all` enables every supported language.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:59:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:60:`lexicon scan` replaces the private source mirror with the repository's current relevant files. The private Git repository supplies the diff from the last successful scan. For ordinary source-file modifications, Lexicon expands changed paths through the previous snapshot's reverse dependency graph, requests incremental JSONL records for that impacted file set, parses the stream once at the adapter boundary, writes replacement per-file objects, reuses every unaffected manifest entry, and publishes a new immutable snapshot. Structural changes and adapter fingerprint changes use complete-language analysis.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:61:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:62:`lexicon demon` watches the repository recursively and invokes the same scan transaction after a debounce. A periodic complete reconciliation repairs missed filesystem events.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:63:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:64:`lexicon rebuild` forces complete analysis of all enabled detected languages or an explicit enabled subset. `lexicon languages set` updates the configured selection, removes disabled language entries from the snapshot, scans immediately, and publishes the result.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:65:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:66:`lexicon status` reports the repository, current snapshot, detected and enabled languages, and consumers. `lexicon doctor` verifies configuration, private Git state, immutable objects, adapter paths, runtime requirements, and consumer commands.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:67:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:68:`lexicon export` reconstructs verified standalone JSONL libraries. `lexicon gc` deletes only unreachable snapshots and objects while preserving retention and consumer pins. Consumer commands manage and invoke deterministic post-publication hooks.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:69:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:70:## Private state repository
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:71:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:72:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:73:.lexicon/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:74:    config.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:75:    CURRENT
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:76:    LOCK
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:77:    PENDING              # transient crash-recovery record
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:78:    consumers/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:79:        arcana.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:80:    consumer-state/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:81:        arcana.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:82:    objects/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:83:        ab/cdef...
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:84:    snapshots/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:85:        <snapshot-id>.json
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:86:    repo/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:87:        .git/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:88:        source/
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:89:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:90:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:91:The state commit is always amended and remains a parentless root commit, so only one commit is reachable. Reflogs are expired after replacement. The repository is an implementation detail used to answer one question: what source content changed since Lexicon last successfully published a snapshot?
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:92:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:93:Each snapshot manifest records the internal state commit, adapter and schema versions, configuration identity, source-content identity, and fact-object identity for every relevant file. Shared synthetic facts are stored in a separate language object. Objects and snapshot manifests are immutable; identical content reuses the existing object. Fact objects use Lexicon's deterministic binary v1 codec with a shared string table and independently length-prefixed node, edge, and unresolved sections. JSONL is reconstructed only by `lexicon export`; snapshot consumers can skip unused binary sections and attributes.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:94:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:95:`CURRENT` contains the complete snapshot ID and is replaced atomically only after the internal state commit and every referenced object are durable. Consumers should resolve `CURRENT`, load the corresponding manifest, and then open its objects. They never need to observe the mutable mirror or adapter JSONL transport files.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:96:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:97:## Object garbage collection
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:98:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:99:Objectstore garbage collection retains the snapshot named by `CURRENT` and the configured number of newest snapshot manifests. It also retains every snapshot named by a `snapshot_id` field in `.lexicon/consumer-state/*.json`; those pins protect consumer work that still refers to an older immutable snapshot. A pinned snapshot that is missing, or a pin file that is malformed or lacks a valid `snapshot_id`, is a hard error and aborts collection.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:100:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:101:The planner follows every preserved manifest's file and shared-object references. Execution deletes only unreferenced snapshot manifests and fact objects. Planning and deletion are deterministic, and execution rejects a plan if `CURRENT` changed after planning. `Store.GarbageCollect(options, dryRun)` performs the bounded plan-and-execute transaction; `dryRun` returns the same deletion lists without removing any files. The explicit planning and execution methods remain available when callers need to inspect a plan before applying it.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:102:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:103:## Snapshot export
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:104:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:105:The `lexicon export` command and objectstore export API write standalone language libraries without changing the current snapshot:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:106:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:107:```text
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:108:lexicon export --output /tmp/lexicon-export --languages python,go
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:109:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:110:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:111:```go
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:112:err := (objectstore.Store{Root: "/repo/.lexicon"}).Export(
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:113:    "CURRENT", "/tmp/lexicon-export", []string{"python", "go"},
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:114:)
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:115:```
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:116:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:117:The snapshot argument may be `CURRENT`, an exact snapshot ID, or empty (which
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:118:also resolves `CURRENT`). An empty language list exports every language;
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:119:requested languages must exist in the manifest. Each selected language becomes
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:120:`<language>.jsonl` in the destination. Export reconstructs the full header from
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:121:manifest metadata, verifies every referenced object, combines shared and
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:122:per-file records, sorts records deterministically, and atomically replaces each
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:123:destination file.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:124:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:125:## Transaction and recovery
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:126:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:127:Only one process may update a repository at a time. Manual scans and demon updates acquire the same advisory lock; a competing writer receives an explicit busy error.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:128:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:129:Before advancing the private state commit, Lexicon writes a durable `PENDING` record containing the complete candidate manifest and whether the source commit must advance. If a process stops before the commit, the next scan discards that candidate and recomputes it. If the commit succeeded but publication did not, the next scan attaches the committed state ID to the pending manifest and atomically publishes it without rerunning adapters. Publications that do not require a source commit, such as adapter-only rebuilds, are also recoverable from `PENDING`.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:130:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:131:Existing installations that still contain committed `.lexicon/repo/library/*.jsonl` files are migrated once into snapshot objects when necessary, after which the materialized directory is removed from the private state commit. New scans never create it.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:132:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:133:## Incremental boundary
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:134:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:135:A modified source file starts an impacted-file object update rather than a complete language rewrite. Lexicon reads the previous immutable snapshot, follows cross-file edges in reverse, and includes every transitive dependent. Files that previously contained unresolved relationships are also included conservatively because a newly introduced declaration may resolve them.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:136:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:137:Lexicon builds a temporary scoped repository containing the impacted files, their transitive forward dependencies from the previous snapshot, and the language's configuration files. Go scopes expand to complete packages and Rust scopes expand to complete crates because those are their minimum sound semantic units. The adapter emits only records owned by the impacted files. Shared synthetic records from the scoped view are marked partial and are not allowed to replace the previous complete shared set.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:138:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:139:A directly edited file that already owns cross-file or unresolved relationships uses complete-language analysis immediately, because a partial candidate universe could preserve the same edge identity while changing its true resolution. Leaf and local-only files use the scoped path. Before applying a scoped result, Lexicon compares emitted edge and unresolved topology with the previous file objects. A new relationship, a new unresolved reference, or a scoped adapter failure automatically retries the complete language repository. When the scoped result is accepted, unaffected file objects remain byte-identical and are reused.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:140:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:141:Additions, deletions, renames, copies, language configuration changes, missing prior dependency data, and invalid prior snapshot state trigger a complete rebuild of the affected language. This is a correctness boundary, not a permanent protocol limitation. The incremental contract already carries removed-file scopes, so future dependency metadata can narrow those cases without changing consumers or snapshot storage.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:142:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:143:## Watch behavior
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:144:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:145:The demon ignores Git metadata, Lexicon state, linked worktrees, dependency directories, and build outputs. An optional repository-root `.lexiconignore` adds gitignore-compatible patterns, including comments, globs, `**`, path hierarchy, and `!` negation, on top of those permanent exclusions. Ignored files are omitted from complete mirror scans, path syncs, and demon watch filtering. Permanent exclusions cannot be re-included by `.lexiconignore`; they include `.git/`, `.worktrees/`, `.workingtrees/`, the Warlock state directories, `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `target/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `__pycache__/`, and `.pytest_cache/`.
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:146:
lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:147:The demon keeps the loaded ignore policy in memory while processing filesystem events. A change to `.lexiconignore` reloads the policy, refreshes recursive watches, and triggers a complete scan. New directories are watched recursively. Deletes and renames remove their mirrored paths. Watcher errors trigger an immediate full reconciliation, and the configured reconciliation interval provides an additional recovery path.

docs/reference/installation.md:1:# Installation and agent setup
docs/reference/installation.md:2:
docs/reference/installation.md:3:This page covers release installation, source builds, command verification, agent skill installation, MCP configuration, first-run state preparation, and common setup failures.
docs/reference/installation.md:4:
docs/reference/installation.md:5:## Recommended release installation
docs/reference/installation.md:6:
docs/reference/installation.md:7:Download and extract the combined release bundle for the target platform:
docs/reference/installation.md:8:
docs/reference/installation.md:9:```text
docs/reference/installation.md:10:grimoire-bundle-<version>-<platform>-<arch>.zip
docs/reference/installation.md:11:```
docs/reference/installation.md:12:
docs/reference/installation.md:13:The bundle contains:
docs/reference/installation.md:14:
docs/reference/installation.md:15:```text
docs/reference/installation.md:16:bin/                    Grimoire, Lexicon, and Arcana executables
docs/reference/installation.md:17:native/                 Lodestone native library
docs/reference/installation.md:18:adapters/               Lexicon runtime adapters
docs/reference/installation.md:19:skills/grimoire/        Canonical Grimoire agent skill
docs/reference/installation.md:20:install.py              Standalone installer
docs/reference/installation.md:21:VERSION                  Bundle version
docs/reference/installation.md:22:```
docs/reference/installation.md:23:
docs/reference/installation.md:24:Run the installer from the extracted bundle:
docs/reference/installation.md:25:
docs/reference/installation.md:26:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:27:python install.py --bin-dir /path/on/your/PATH
docs/reference/installation.md:28:```
docs/reference/installation.md:29:
docs/reference/installation.md:30:On Windows, `py -3` may be the configured launcher:
docs/reference/installation.md:31:
docs/reference/installation.md:32:```powershell
docs/reference/installation.md:33:py -3 install.py --bin-dir "$HOME\bin"
docs/reference/installation.md:34:```
docs/reference/installation.md:35:
docs/reference/installation.md:36:The installer does not modify `PATH`. Add the selected binary directory through the operating system or shell configuration.
docs/reference/installation.md:37:
docs/reference/installation.md:38:### Component selection
docs/reference/installation.md:39:
docs/reference/installation.md:40:Omitting `--component` installs all three applications. Repeat the option to install a subset:
docs/reference/installation.md:41:
docs/reference/installation.md:42:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:43:python install.py --bin-dir /path/on/your/PATH --component grimoire
docs/reference/installation.md:44:python install.py --bin-dir /path/on/your/PATH --component lexicon --component arcana
docs/reference/installation.md:45:```
docs/reference/installation.md:46:
docs/reference/installation.md:47:Selecting Grimoire also installs its required Lodestone native library and agent skill. Selecting Lexicon also installs its runtime adapters.
docs/reference/installation.md:48:
docs/reference/installation.md:49:### Skill installation
docs/reference/installation.md:50:
docs/reference/installation.md:51:By default, a Grimoire installation writes the canonical skill to both supported user roots:
docs/reference/installation.md:52:
docs/reference/installation.md:53:```text
docs/reference/installation.md:54:~/.agents/skills/grimoire/SKILL.md
docs/reference/installation.md:55:~/.hermes/skills/grimoire/SKILL.md
docs/reference/installation.md:56:```
docs/reference/installation.md:57:
docs/reference/installation.md:58:Override the roots by repeating `--skills-dir`:
docs/reference/installation.md:59:
docs/reference/installation.md:60:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:61:python install.py --bin-dir /path/on/your/PATH \
docs/reference/installation.md:62:  --skills-dir /first/agent/skills \
docs/reference/installation.md:63:  --skills-dir /second/agent/skills
docs/reference/installation.md:64:```
docs/reference/installation.md:65:
docs/reference/installation.md:66:Install only binaries and runtime files with:
docs/reference/installation.md:67:
docs/reference/installation.md:68:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:69:python install.py --bin-dir /path/on/your/PATH --skip-skills
docs/reference/installation.md:70:```
docs/reference/installation.md:71:
docs/reference/installation.md:72:Start a new agent session after installing or updating a skill so the host can rediscover it.
docs/reference/installation.md:73:
docs/reference/installation.md:74:## Verify the installation
docs/reference/installation.md:75:
docs/reference/installation.md:76:Run:
docs/reference/installation.md:77:
docs/reference/installation.md:78:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:79:grimoire version
docs/reference/installation.md:80:grimoire lexicon check
docs/reference/installation.md:81:grimoire arcana check
docs/reference/installation.md:82:grimoire help
docs/reference/installation.md:83:```
docs/reference/installation.md:84:
docs/reference/installation.md:85:Expected behavior:
docs/reference/installation.md:86:
docs/reference/installation.md:87:- `grimoire version` reports the installed release or development version;
docs/reference/installation.md:88:- `lexicon check` reports the resolved Lexicon command and version;
docs/reference/installation.md:89:- `arcana check` reports the resolved Arcana command and version;
docs/reference/installation.md:90:- `grimoire help` lists direct discovery, MCP, state, vector, model, investigation, and engine namespace commands.
docs/reference/installation.md:91:
docs/reference/installation.md:92:When provider discovery fails, verify that all bundle executables were installed together or use the explicit environment overrides documented in [CLI environment variables](cli.md#environment-variables).
docs/reference/installation.md:93:
docs/reference/installation.md:94:## Prepare a repository
docs/reference/installation.md:95:
docs/reference/installation.md:96:Grimoire stores repository-owned prepared state and refreshes it on demand. Check and prepare the current repository with:
docs/reference/installation.md:97:
docs/reference/installation.md:98:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:99:grimoire status --root . --refresh
docs/reference/installation.md:100:```
docs/reference/installation.md:101:
docs/reference/installation.md:102:Then run a narrow code-first search:
docs/reference/installation.md:103:
docs/reference/installation.md:104:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:105:grimoire search \
docs/reference/installation.md:106:  --root . \
docs/reference/installation.md:107:  --query "Where is session creation handled?" \
docs/reference/installation.md:108:  --code-only \
docs/reference/installation.md:109:  --limit 6 \
docs/reference/installation.md:110:  --session session-flow
docs/reference/installation.md:111:```
docs/reference/installation.md:112:
docs/reference/installation.md:113:The first preparation can cost more than later queries because Grimoire may need to align source, Lexicon, Arcana, and documentation state. Normal discovery uses `refresh-if-needed`; do not use `force-refresh` as a routine first step.
docs/reference/installation.md:114:
docs/reference/installation.md:115:## Configure an agent host
docs/reference/installation.md:116:
docs/reference/installation.md:117:Grimoire serves one stdio MCP tool:
docs/reference/installation.md:118:
docs/reference/installation.md:119:```bash
docs/reference/installation.md:120:grimoire mcp --root /absolute/path/to/repository
docs/reference/installation.md:121:```
docs/reference/installation.md:122:
docs/reference/installation.md:123:Configure the host with the equivalent command and arguments:
docs/reference/installation.md:124:
docs/reference/installation.md:125:```json
docs/reference/installation.md:126:{
docs/reference/installation.md:127:  "command": "grimoire",
docs/reference/installation.md:128:  "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/absolute/path/to/repository"]
docs/reference/installation.md:129:}
docs/reference/installation.md:130:```
docs/reference/installation.md:131:
docs/reference/installation.md:132:The surrounding MCP configuration object is host-specific. Keep the repository path absolute when the host may launch the process from another working directory.
docs/reference/installation.md:133:
docs/reference/installation.md:134:The server exposes:
docs/reference/installation.md:135:
docs/reference/installation.md:136:```text
docs/reference/installation.md:137:grimoire_discover
docs/reference/installation.md:138:```
docs/reference/installation.md:139:
docs/reference/installation.md:140:The installed skill and MCP tool are complementary:
docs/reference/installation.md:141:
docs/reference/installation.md:142:- the skill teaches the agent when and how to use Grimoire efficiently;
docs/reference/installation.md:143:- the MCP server executes the unified discovery contract;
docs/reference/installation.md:144:- normal shell, Git, search, and file-reading tools remain available for direct verification.
docs/reference/installation.md:145:
docs/reference/installation.md:146:Do not restrict an agent to Grimoire alone. The intended operating model is Grimoire-assisted repository inspection.

docs/reference/cli.md:310:## Environment variables

301:
302:## `grimoire version`
303:
304:```bash
305:grimoire version
306:```
307:
308:Release builds override the development version through linker flags.
309:
310:## Environment variables
311:
312:Provider and embedding configuration is documented with the owning component. Common discovery does not require environment variables when the consolidated binaries are installed together.
313:
314:`GRIMOIRE_HOME` may identify the consolidated checkout for provider discovery. Repository-local `.grimoire/providers.json` can pin Lexicon and Arcana commands. `GRIMOIRE_LEXICON_COMMAND` and `GRIMOIRE_ARCANA_COMMAND` override command discovery for the corresponding namespaced engine commands.
315:
316:## Error behavior
317:
318:- Invalid requests fail before querying.
319:- Stale handles fail rather than being fuzzily rediscovered.
320:- Missing structural providers produce warnings while source and document discovery continue when possible.
321:- Missing or stale documentation vectors fall back to BM25.
322:- A repository that cannot produce current source state fails discovery instead of returning stale implementation evidence.
323:
324:## Related documentation
325:
326:- [Unified discovery contract](agent-query.md)
327:- [Grimoire MCP interface](agent-mcp.md)
328:- [System overview](../architecture/system-overview.md)
329:- [Current limitations](../limits/current-limitations.md)

51:	direction := flags.String("direction", "", "graph direction: incoming, outgoing, or both")
52:	adjacent := flags.Int("adjacent-context", 0, "source lines adjacent to an inspected declaration")
53:	codeOnly := flags.Bool("code-only", false, "omit the documentation lane")
54:	includeDocumentsValue := true
55:	flags.BoolVar(&includeDocumentsValue, "include-documents", true, "include separately ranked documentation matches")
56:	documentVectors := flags.Bool("document-vectors", false, "use available documentation vectors in addition to BM25")
57:	detail := flags.String("detail", "", "response detail: default previews or full inline evidence")
58:	requestJSON := flags.String("request", "", "complete "+agentquery.SchemaVersion+" JSON request object")
59:	lexiconFacts := flags.String("lexicon-facts", "", "explicit directory containing exported Lexicon JSONL libraries")

61:	lexiconCommand := flags.String("lexicon-command", "", "Lexicon executable override; discovered when omitted")

63:	arcanaCommand := flags.String("arcana-command", "", "Arcana executable override; discovered when omitted")

68:	flags.Var(&relations, "relation", "graph relation filter; may be repeated")

117:				ArcanaCmd:    *arcanaCommand,

docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:20:## Lexical-first source discovery
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:22:Prepared source state now includes a persistent identifier-aware lexical index. Source discovery uses postings to localize candidate chunks before BM25 scoring rather than rescanning the entire prepared corpus for each query.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:59:The root workflow remains CPU-bounded by default across Go and Cargo. Release archives are deterministic and the GitHub release workflow publishes Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 combined bundles. The embedded bundle installer now copies Lexicon runtime adapters, and a release-consumer smoke packages a real combined ZIP, installs it into a clean temporary location, launches the installed MCP server, prepares managed provider state, and verifies opaque handles through inspect and trace.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:108:- HikariCP connection lifecycle: plain 6m 32s, Grimoire 13m 19s, CBM 16m 18s;
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:116:## Benchmark hardening and preparation telemetry
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:122:Repository preparation status now separates initial inspection, lock wait, reinspection, Lexicon, Arcana, source indexing, documentation indexing, marker writes, final source verification, and total time. The refresh path reuses one post-lock source fingerprint through provider preparation instead of repeatedly walking the repository after each action, then performs one final fingerprint check before marking state current.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:126:The first version 2 architecture run produced grounded implementation-grade answers in all three conditions. Grimoire completed in 6m 36s with 16 calls and 1.05M total tokens, versus CBM at 11m 33s/25 calls/3.30M tokens and plain at 12m 27s/18 calls/1.84M tokens. Grimoire cold preparation took 95.2 seconds, dominated by 69.3 seconds of Lexicon work. The run also exposed and fixed validator support for noncontiguous structured ranges; saved outputs can now be revalidated without rerunning agents.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:128:The second version 2 Detekt run also produced grounded implementation-grade answers in all three conditions, but plain inspection won: 5m 04s, 14 calls, and 767k total tokens. CBM was effectively tied at 5m 05s including preparation, 16 calls, and 831k tokens. Grimoire took 6m 26s including preparation, 16 calls, and 1.46M tokens. All three found the same Gradle-to-CLI plugin-classloader defect and proposed the same adapter-layer repair. Grimoire's single 44.9 KB search response began with low-value import nodes, confirming that broad response shaping can still add cost after the task's working set becomes compact.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:132:The third version 2 locator run favored plain inspection and CBM over Grimoire. Plain completed in 5m 27s with 21 calls and 2.18M total tokens; CBM completed in 6m 37s including preparation with 25 calls and 2.40M tokens; Grimoire completed in 9m 41s including preparation with 21 calls and 2.38M tokens. Plain and CBM chose a dedicated unreliable locator packet, while Grimoire reused the reliable overlay lane for changing coordinates and omitted stale expiry. All three missed durable per-player color metadata and complete spectating verification despite passing citation grounding.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:136:The fourth version 2 LevelDB task was won by CBM: 4m 52s including preparation, 10 calls, and 495k total tokens. Plain produced a strong valid answer in 6m 43s with 12 calls and 598k tokens.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:138:The original Grimoire condition ran without Arcana because the C-family `unsupported-macro-expansion` reason was missing from Arcana's enum. It took 6m 41s including preparation, used 16 calls and 1.57M tokens, expanded 138 KB of fallback discovery output, and failed three canonical handle/range checks.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:140:After the compatibility fix, the Grimoire-only rerun completed with Lexicon and Arcana current and aligned. It took 5m 45s including preparation, used 17 calls and 1.29M tokens, and made one 32 KB search call. The answer now found the queued-callback race and proposed gating both scheduling and callback execution, but retained unsafe idempotent boolean ownership semantics. It was still automatically invalidated because one narrower evidence range did not match its broader canonical handle.
docs/development/recent-changes-2026-07.md:146:The README now starts with release installation, first use, and agent configuration rather than developer build internals. New documentation covers:

## Recommendation

Split ownership at the semantic boundary:

- **Warlock should own the long-lived repository watcher and lifecycle supervision**: repository registration, OS watches, debounce/coalescing, overflow recovery, periodic reconciliation, process health, retry/backoff, and fan-out to interested tools.
- **Grimoire should own interpretation of a change and the resulting state transaction**: freshness validation, Lexicon refresh, Arcana alignment, prepared-source rebuild, documentation indexing, snapshot validation, and degradation policy.
- Raw events should be **hints, not proof of freshness**. Grimoire must continue validating repository and snapshot identities itself.
- Preserve the existing standalone path: every one-shot query and `status --refresh` must remain able to prepare state without Warlock.

This avoids making Grimoire a second lifecycle supervisor while retaining its existing ownership of cross-provider consistency.

## Verified current behavior

At checked-out revision `0375e5f6e541970e6ef509ac655961405c82e0f3`:

1. Every discovery execution normalizes the request, invokes repository preparation before querying, and refuses to query unless deterministic source state is ready. The default state mode is `refresh-if-needed`, so standalone calls already repair stale state on demand (`internal/agentruntime/runtime.go:20-61`, `internal/agentruntime/runtime.go:157-186`).

2. Grimoire’s preparation transaction is already the correct semantic consumer for a repository-change notification:

   - inspect current state;
   - take an in-process and cross-process refresh lock;
   - reinspect after waiting;
   - refresh or initialize Lexicon;
   - synchronize Arcana to Lexicon;
   - rebuild Grimoire source state;
   - rebuild documentation state;
   - verify that source did not change during preparation (`internal/repostate/ensure.go:20-83`, `internal/repostate/ensure.go:84-188`).

   The implementation deliberately serializes callers and rechecks after the lock, so concurrent query and background refresh requests converge rather than independently rebuilding (`internal/repostate/ensure.go:63-83`). Tests verify both ordered provider preparation and single-flight behavior (`internal/repostate/repostate_test.go:303-320`, `internal/repostate/repostate_test.go:471-496`).

3. Repository changes during preparation are rejected instead of publishing apparently current state (`internal/repostate/ensure.go:170-185`). The corresponding test mutates the repository during document preparation and verifies that readiness is withheld (`internal/repostate/repostate_test.go:273-301`).

4. Grimoire freshness is snapshot- and fingerprint-based, not event-based. Inspection validates the repository fingerprint, Lexicon snapshot, Arcana-to-Lexicon alignment, prepared-source marker, and documentation fingerprint (`internal/repostate/inspect.go:65-107`, `internal/repostate/inspect.go:112-214`, `internal/repostate/inspect.go:217-236`). This is the correctness mechanism that must remain authoritative after watching is introduced.

5. The current “all deterministic state is current” fast path includes Lexicon, Arcana, prepared source, and documentation (`internal/repostate/current.go:3-7`). Consequently, cold discovery can prepare documentation even for an ultimately code-only query: preparation occurs before document-lane selection, and `Ensure` refreshes knowledge whenever it is stale (`internal/agentruntime/runtime.go:39-55`, `internal/repostate/ensure.go:151-169`).

6. Grimoire’s source and documentation builders are incremental in materialization but still traverse their eligible trees. The source builder reuses records only when content, size, and semantic-preparation identity match; changed records are rechunked (`internal/index/build.go:58-75`, `internal/index/build.go:77-174`). Documentation similarly reuses unchanged documents by content hash and size (`internal/knowledge/discover.go:33-60`, `internal/knowledge/discover.go:60-145`). Prewarming therefore moves substantial traversal/provider work off the first query without requiring event-perfect incremental updates.

7. The implemented long-lived filesystem watcher belongs to Lexicon, not Grimoire. `lexicon demon` constructs a scanner and enters the watch loop (`lexicon/internal/cli/cli.go:136-155`). The watcher performs a startup scan, debounces path events into `ScanPaths`, falls back to full scans for control-file changes or watcher errors, and periodically reconciles the entire repository (`lexicon/internal/watch/daemon.go:24-53`, `lexicon/internal/watch/daemon.go:54-140`).

8. Lexicon’s watcher is intentionally coupled only to Lexicon’s scan transaction. Both full and path-scoped scans invoke registered one-shot consumers after a successful scan (`lexicon/internal/scan/scanner.go:35-52`). Consumer commands are external processes with optional timeouts and immutable snapshot identity in their environment (`lexicon/internal/consumer/runner.go:27-61`, `lexicon/internal/consumer/runner.go:83-117`). It does not update Grimoire’s source or document indexes itself.

9. Grimoire already accepts explicit state roots for all three components, and tests exercise `.warlock/tools/{lexicon,arcana,grimoire}` without creating default `.lexicon` state (`internal/repostate/types.go:25-36`, `internal/repostate/inspect.go:35-58`, `internal/repostate/repostate_test.go:322-370`). However, the current `status` command exposes no corresponding state-root flags, so it is not yet a complete Warlock maintenance surface (`internal/app/status.go:14-44`). Direct discovery does expose `--state`, `--lexicon-state`, and `--arcana-state` (`internal/app/query.go:39-64`, `internal/app/query.go:96-123`).

10. A subtle duplication hazard already exists: after successfully refreshing Lexicon, `Ensure` sets `lexiconChanged`, reinspects, and synchronizes Arcana whenever that flag is true—even if a registered Lexicon consumer has already brought Arcana current (`internal/repostate/ensure.go:94-116`, `internal/repostate/ensure.go:116-135`). Warlock therefore should not independently run Lexicon’s daemon/Arcana hook and Grimoire’s whole alignment transaction for the same managed repository.

## Proposed design

### Warlock-owned event source

Maintain one watcher per registered repository. Its responsibilities should be limited to:

- recursive OS watching;
- repository startup/shutdown and process supervision;
- debouncing and coalescing;
- detecting watcher overflow and requesting full reconciliation;
- periodic reconciliation;
- retry/backoff after failed maintenance;
- retaining the newest unprocessed repository generation while maintenance is running.

A useful event envelope would include the canonical repository root, a monotonically increasing local generation, cause (`startup`, `filesystem`, `reconcile`, `overflow`), and optional normalized repository-relative paths. Paths must remain optimization hints; Warlock should not duplicate Grimoire, Lexicon, or documentation ignore/eligibility policy.

If another event arrives during preparation, Warlock should mark a newer generation pending. If Grimoire reports “source changed during preparation,” retry the newest generation immediately rather than treating it as persistent failure.

### Grimoire-owned event application

Add a bounded, non-resident maintenance surface—either a dedicated `grimoire maintain` command or state-complete `status --refresh` flags—that accepts:

- `--root`;
- `--state`;
- `--lexicon-state`;
- `--arcana-state`;
- provider command overrides;
- optional event generation and changed-path hints.

Its correctness path should call the existing `repostate.Ensure(...RefreshIfNeeded...)`. Do not construct a parallel event-specific provider pipeline.

Initially, changed paths need not alter preparation semantics. Existing fingerprints, Lexicon incremental scanning, source-record reuse, and document reuse already provide correctness. Later, path hints can avoid unrelated work, but classification should remain inside Grimoire/provider-owned packages.

Two near-term refinements are warranted:

- After Lexicon refresh and reinspection, synchronize Arcana only if it is still stale; this prevents duplicate sync when a standalone Lexicon consumer already handled it.
- Split coarse freshness identities if measurements show documentation-only changes unnecessarily refreshing Lexicon. The present repository fingerprint includes both source and documentation/configuration extensions (`internal/repostate/fingerprint.go:177-197`), so event classification alone cannot safely skip work without corresponding freshness-state changes.

Return the existing structured actions, timing buckets, warnings, component snapshots, and readiness result to Warlock. Warlock should record these as lifecycle health but must not reinterpret partial provider warnings as state identities.

### Standalone preservation

Keep all existing one-shot behavior:

- Discovery remains `refresh-if-needed` by default.
- `current-only` remains an explicit optimization/assertion, not a Warlock-only requirement.
- `status --refresh` remains usable with no daemon.
- `lexicon demon` remains available for standalone Lexicon installations.
- Explicit `arcana sync` remains able to catch up from immutable Lexicon state.
- Watch notifications never replace fingerprint or snapshot validation.
- Do not automatically rebuild optional vectors on every edit; deterministic source/document preparation and vector lifecycle should remain separate.

In a Warlock-managed repository, Warlock should invoke the single Grimoire maintenance transaction and should not also launch `lexicon demon`. In standalone mode, Lexicon’s existing watcher and consumers remain untouched.

## Documentation rationale

The repository documentation already points toward this split, but these are design intentions rather than proof of implementation:

- The roadmap explicitly calls for “optional repository watching or Warlock-fed change events” without making one-shot commands daemon-dependent (`docs/planning/roadmap.md:44-50`).
- It separately calls for Warlock lifecycle integration while preserving independently usable components (`docs/planning/roadmap.md:70-77`).
- Current limitations identify request-driven maintenance and cold alignment cost as the existing problem (`docs/limits/current-limitations.md:85-89`).
- The documented component boundary assigns Grimoire repository-state preparation while retaining separate provider executables and state lifecycles (`arcana/README.md:10-27`).
- Lexicon’s documentation describes its demon as merely an event-to-scan adapter and states that snapshot consumers do not depend on it (`lexicon/docs/APPLICATION.md:5-10`).
- The prepared-index package documentation explicitly excludes daemon lifecycle and file watching from index ownership (`internal/index/README.md:22-28`).

The resulting rule is: **Warlock owns when maintenance is attempted; Grimoire owns what “current and aligned” means.**
